name: CJC-1295 with DAC

lead: CJC-1295 with DAC is a long-acting version of a GHRH analogue, meant to make the pituitary release more growth hormone. Forum users pair it with ipamorelin or tesamorelin for muscle and body-composition goals.
The community material is thin and anecdotal, and there are no cited trials of it for appearance.

paras: It mimics GHRH at the pituitary, and the DAC attachment binds blood proteins to prolong its action versus the version without DAC.
It is not an approved medicine and risks in healthy users have not been defined by the sources used here. Forum discussions focus on combinations rather than safety data.

lead: CJC-1295 with DAC is a synthetic analogue of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) that carries a drug affinity complex (DAC), a chemical attachment intended to bind blood proteins and prolong its action compared with shorter-acting GHRH analogues. It was developed by the Canadian company ConjuChem Biotechnologies and has not been approved as a medicine.

In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding communities it is discussed as a growth hormone secretagogue for muscle, body composition and recovery, often together with a growth hormone-releasing peptide such as ipamorelin or with tesamorelin. [1] The community material available is limited to a small number of forum exchanges, in which users disagree about whether the DAC version or the version without DAC is preferable. [1]
No published human trials of its effect on appearance, muscle or body composition are cited here, so its appearance-related evidence is regarded as unproven.
infobox: CJC-1295 without DAC (modified GRF 1-29), tesamorelin, ipamorelin

paras: A looksmax.org thread asks whether combining tesamorelin, CJC-1295 DAC and ipamorelin is dangerous and whether it is better than pairing CJC-1295 DAC with ipamorelin alone. The original poster says they know more about surgeries than about peptides or steroids. [1]

A reply in that thread argues there is no point in stacking several GHRH analogues and GHRPs and recommends the variant without DAC with ipamorelin instead; the original poster responds that they had assumed more GHRH analogues would give a better result. [1] These are individual opinions and do not reflect any published comparison.

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, CJC-1295 DAC appears in peptide-stack questions, usually alongside ipamorelin or tesamorelin. [1]

claims.claim: Using several GHRH analogues together gives a better result than one
The version without DAC combined with ipamorelin is preferable to the DAC version
